resources.string: Turn USB debugging on and off with one tap
ADB Switch needs setup. Tap to open the guide.
The widget is ready to use.
Follow the steps marked below. This screen re-checks every time you come back.
Tapping the widget opens this guide and nothing changes.
Android only allows granting this permission from a computer. Connect the phone with USB debugging on and run this command once (again after reinstalling the app):
The widget always shows Disabled, even when debugging is on.
This phone does not expose the state of the adb service, and there is no fix on the phone side. Report your model and Android version so support can be added.
Tapping the widget does not turn debugging back on (it returns to OFF). Ignore this if you just turned it off with the widget.
Developer options are probably disabled. Open About phone, tap Build number 7 times, then turn on USB debugging in Developer options.
This screen is not available on this phone
The widget is not on any home screen yet.
Long-press the home screen → Widgets → ADB Switch, or use the button.

string-array.name: faq_symptoms
string-array.item: Tapping the widget opens this guide
The computer disconnects when I turn debugging off
The widget shows Enabled but USB debugging is off
The widget shows the wrong state after changing it in Settings
The widget turns itself back to OFF

string-array.name: faq_fixes
string-array.item: The permission is missing, usually after reinstalling. Run the adb command shown above.
Expected: turning USB debugging off closes every adb connection.
Wireless debugging is on and keeps the adb service running. Turn it off in Developer options.
The widget only updates when tapped. Tap it, or open this app to refresh it.
Developer options are disabled. Enable them (Build number ×7) and try again.
